examples.title: Search component properties
examples.description: Search component names, properties, quantities, materials and classifications, then show only the matching components.
examples.guideHtml:
Search component properties

Search component names, properties, quantities, materials and classifications, then show only the matching components.

Search

Enter a name, property name or value and press Search or Enter to isolate matching components. Search is case-insensitive; every space-separated word must occur in the same component. GlobalIds remain searchable. A search with no matches hides all components; an empty search restores the full model. To inspect properties, click a visible component, then click 1 element selected at the top left to open Properties. If loading fails, click Search to retry.

Developer integration

The page queries all products through the published viewer.IfcAPI, including occurrence and inherited type properties, quantities, materials and classifications. Shared definitions are read once in bounded batches. The original West Riverside Hospital architectural model is hash-verified. Search results are isolated through BCF visibility exceptions using bcf.save(), viewer.add() and viewer.selectTopic(). The viewpoint preserves the camera and does not select or color components. Loading and errors use the viewer message API.

The page opens the original source bytes with await viewer.IfcAPI, reads native model data, then closes the model and disposes WASM before displaying the source with viewer.add(). See the complete web-ifc API reference.

examples.guideHtml:
Open saved floor plans by storey

Choose a storey to open its saved floor plan, then pan and zoom to inspect the layout.

BIM workflow

Choose any storey returned by the model. The lowest storey opens first. Each button restores a top-down floor slice; pan and zoom to inspect the plan. The left toolbar's Sections panel shows the recognized storey and cut. Select a component and click 1 element selected at the top left to open Properties.

Developer integration

An integration supplies each saved floor plan as a downward BCF camera and two horizontal clipping bounds. The page queries storey names and placements through viewer.IfcAPI. Cuts retain 0.30 m below each queried elevation and 1.50 m above it. bcf.save(), viewer.add() and viewer.selectTopic() handle the saved views; the model is imported once and plan changes select an existing topic.

Copy this folder and serve it over HTTP, for example python -m http.server 8080. Open http://localhost:8080/; the SDK and sample downloads require internet access.

The page opens the original source bytes with await viewer.IfcAPI, reads native model data, then closes the model and disposes WASM before displaying the source with viewer.add(). See the complete web-ifc API reference.

examples.title: Check wall names and fire-rating information
examples.description: Run IDS checks to find walls with missing names or fire-rating values, then highlight passing or failing components.
examples.guideHtml:
Check wall names and fire-rating information

Run IDS checks to find walls with missing names or fire-rating values, then highlight passing or failing components.

Try it

The example opens the three discipline models with their original appearance and loads the two IDS specifications, ready for you to run.

Open IDS (circled check) on the left toolbar and click Run All Checks. Expand Walls · fire-rating information, then click Apply beside a failed finding to highlight those walls in red, or beside Passed elements to highlight passing walls in green. The SDK applies each finding separately. Click a wall, then click 1 element selected at the top left to open Properties and inspect Pset_WallCommon.FireRating.

Expected results

The fire-rating information check finds 299 passing structural walls with FireRating = 120, and 353 failing facade walls: 351 have no FireRating property and two have an empty value. The wall-name check finds 301 passing and 351 failing walls. The stairs model contains no applicable walls. These results come from the unchanged source exports.

Developer integration

Two IDS specifications are embedded alongside the three original IFC discipline models. The SDK runs the IDS checks. Use Run All Checks in the IDS panel to evaluate the loaded models, then Apply on a finding to visualize its results. The example does not calculate separate results or create a BCF overview at startup. Both checks review information completeness. The fire-rating check requires a non-empty Pset_WallCommon.FireRating, not a particular rating; it does not assess fire-safety compliance or represent the project contract.

Serve this folder over HTTP. The published SDK and source downloads require internet access.

Model notes

The original IFC source is imported unchanged.

examples.title: Compare a building model with its scan
examples.description: Compare a building IFC with its matching colour point cloud to inspect façades, balconies and roof edges.
examples.guideHtml:
Compare a building model with its scan

Compare a building IFC with its matching colour point cloud to inspect façades, balconies and roof edges.

Try it

  1. Orbit around the building and inspect roof edges, balconies and end walls.
  2. Open Files (folder) on the left toolbar. Toggle the checkboxes beside the IFC and LAZ files to compare each source with their overlay.
  3. Open Sections (scissors) on the left toolbar → Add clipping plane, then click a surface to inspect the relationship between model and scan.

Source alignment

The pair is example-no-1.ifc and example-no-1.laz from the xeokit examples repository. The scan has 9,265,546 points, including surrounding ground and parked cars. Both files use shared local metre coordinates. The IFC bounds are approximately X 705.512–793.626 m, Y 84.995–109.509 m, Z 82.083–106.356 m, inside the scan bounds X 694.785–802.589 m, Y 78.559–114.389 m, Z 78.515–106.567 m. Rooflines, façades and balconies visually overlap without a translation, rotation or scale correction. This visual check does not certify survey accuracy or model deviations.

Developer integration

The page checks each source’s byte length and SHA-256 before passing the original Blob to viewer.add(name, blob). It loads the IFC first, then the LAZ, retaining successful imports when a later download needs a retry. The SDK handles parsing, point-cloud storage, visibility, sections and navigation. Neither file declares a projected CRS, so the example adds no geographic location or map conversion. The IFC is about 30 MB and the LAZ about 91 MB.

Copy this folder and serve it over HTTP. The published SDK and remote sample downloads require internet access.

examples.guideHtml:
Share a model view with a link

Create a BCF topic from the model view, then share its link or download the BCF file.

Try it

  1. Orbit, pan or zoom to the view you want to share.
  2. Click Create link, then Copy link or Download BCF. Open view reopens the shared BCF topic.
  3. The same pinned model loads and the saved BCF view is restored.

Developer integration

viewer.createTopic(undefined, { snapshot: false }) captures the current view in a BCF 3.0 archive. bcf.save() writes the same standard BCF bytes used by the download and the URL fragment. The optional snapshot is omitted to keep links smaller. bcf.load() validates the archive before viewer.add() and viewer.selectTopic(id) restore it. The URL encoding belongs to this page; the BCF payload follows buildingSMART BCF-XML. Large selections or image attachments can exceed the link limit; download the BCF file in that case.

examples.title: Edit IFC georeferencing with web-ifc
examples.description: Use the native IFC API to position the S1 building and 3DBAG surroundings, then display the edited models on a map.
examples.guideHtml:
Edit IFC georeferencing with web-ifc

Use the native IFC API to position the S1 building and 3DBAG surroundings, then display the edited models on a map.

Try it

  1. Compare the building with the surrounding buildings and street map.
  2. Open Files (folder) on the left toolbar and toggle the checkbox beside OMG_KS_3dBAG.ifc to distinguish project geometry from its neighbours.
  3. Zoom to the project boundary to inspect its relationship to the nearby buildings.

Developer integration

Use const api = await viewer.IfcAPI to obtain the complete native web-ifc instance supplied by the SDK. Call Init() and OpenModel() for each downloaded IFC. This API runs on the main thread and owns its models independently of the viewer.

This example reads the project, site and geometric contexts through web-ifc. It updates the site coordinates and true north, writes the IFC2X3 ePSet_ProjectedCRS and ePSet_MapConversion property sets with CreateIfcEntity(), CreateIfcType() and WriteLine(), then saves the edited bytes with SaveModel().

The native model is closed and WASM disposed before the saved bytes are passed to viewer.add(). After all three files load, viewer.toggleMap(true) displays their corrected placement. Native vectors are released explicitly. Repeated access to viewer.IfcAPI returns the same instance, which is initialized again for the next file. Geometry and local heights are retained, and the original downloads are not overwritten.

See the complete web-ifc API reference for all native methods.

Copy this folder and serve it over HTTP, for example python -m http.server 8080. Open http://localhost:8080/; the SDK and sample downloads require internet access.

Model notes

Georeferencing corrected; geometry retained. Heights are local.

examples.title: Measure and section a point cloud
examples.description: Measure distances between scan points and cut through a site survey to inspect ground, buildings and vegetation.
examples.guideHtml:
Measure and section a point cloud

Measure distances between scan points and cut through a site survey to inspect ground, buildings and vegetation.

Measure site access

  1. Find a street or approach beside the stadium and zoom to its edges.
  2. On the left toolbar, open Measure (ruler) → Add measurement. Set Measure Mode to Length and pick two survey points to measure a route or its width.
  3. Measure a second route to compare the available space.

Inspect a scan section

  1. Find the stadium edge and its surrounding ground.
  2. On the left toolbar, open Sections (scissors) → Add clipping plane, then click a surface to cut through the scan and examine ground and elevated features.
  3. Drag the section to compare nearby buildings and vegetation.

Developer integration

Load the original classified LAZ survey once with viewer.add(). The SDK provides point picking, measurement and section controls for the same scan. Source classification is preserved. The survey was captured in 2010 and classified by Max Sampson, Hobu, Inc. in 2021; these exercises do not represent a current site access assessment.

Copy this folder and serve it over HTTP, for example python -m http.server 8080. Open http://localhost:8080/; the SDK and sample downloads require internet access.

Select elements from a work schedule

Choose a wall-installation activity to highlight the walls assigned to it in the building model.

Developer integration

The page queries walls and their containing storeys through viewer.IfcAPI, then builds a wall-installation activity for each returned storey. Labels, membership and counts come from the loaded model. The click handler builds a selection-only BCF update, writes it with bcf.save(), then applies it with viewer.add() and viewer.selectTopic(). One topic is reused; no camera, colors or visibility filters are supplied.

Find windows by width

Compare window widths against a nominal size threshold and highlight the matching windows.

Review widths

Move the width slider. Amber windows meet the threshold; blue windows are narrower. Select a window, then click 1 element selected at the top left for Properties.

Developer integration

The component identifiers, names, dimensions and memberships are queried through the native viewer.IfcAPI. The original IFC2x3 file is hash-verified and imported unchanged. BCF views are written with bcf.save(), imported with viewer.add(), and applied with viewer.selectTopic(). Open Topics (speech bubble) on the left toolbar to inspect the generated viewpoint.

The page reads each window’s OverallWidth attribute and the project length unit, converts widths to millimetres, then builds the two color sets at runtime.

Show selected components in a table

Click a duct or fitting to see its name, floor and system in a table. Select more components to compare their records.

Try it

Click a duct or fitting. Ctrl/⌘+click adds components to the selection and table.

Developer integration

viewer.onViewChange provides selected GlobalIds. The page resolves them through viewer.IfcAPI.GetExpressIdFromGuid, then queries entity names, storeys and property sets from its independently opened native model. It does not ship a cached property table. An outdated query cannot replace a newer selection.

The page keeps its native IFC model open for selection queries and closes it when the page is unloaded. viewer.clear() controls only the rendered model. Native calls run on the main thread. See the complete web-ifc API reference.

examples.guideHtml:
View a bridge on a map

See how a bridge connects the surrounding roads across a river, and switch between street and satellite maps.

Try it

  1. Use the map to locate the bridge relative to the roads and river.
  2. Open View at the top right → Layers and choose Satellite or Street to compare the model with the surrounding area.
  3. Zoom between the bridge and its wider setting.

Developer integration

After viewer.add(), call viewer.toggleMap(true) to show the project's map context. The SDK owns map styles and terrain controls. The source placement and height limitations are listed under Model notes.

Copy this folder and serve it over HTTP, for example python -m http.server 8080. Open http://localhost:8080/; the SDK and sample downloads require internet access.

The host uses await viewer.IfcAPI to open the hash-verified source, writes the projected CRS vertical datum with WriteLine(), and saves the edited bytes with SaveModel(). It closes the native model and disposes WASM before viewer.add(). See the complete web-ifc API reference.

Model notes

Height datum set to NAP (inferred); geometry retained. The publisher reports a small XYZ offset. Optional terrain is a 30 m surface.

examples.title: Review saved annotations at a stair opening
examples.description: Open an existing BCF outline and arrow in a close section view to review the stair opening and its approach.
examples.guideHtml:
Review saved annotations at a stair opening

Open an existing BCF outline and arrow in a close section view to review the stair opening and its approach.

Try it

The saved viewpoint opens automatically. A rectangle marks the stair opening and an arrow leads from the approach toward the landing. The close oblique section exposes the stair flight, handrail and neighboring rooms. Orbit or zoom to inspect the relationship, then click Restore annotated view to return to the review camera.

Open Topics (speech bubble) on the left toolbar and select Review stair opening protection to read the coordination note. Select a component, then click 1 element selected at the top left to open Properties.

Developer integration

This page imports the full BIM Whale Advanced Project and an existing BCF 3.0 archive embedded in the inline configuration. The archive already contains a bold closed rectangle and arrow built from closely spaced BCF line segments, an orthogonal camera and six clipping planes. The review geometry uses the pinned model's Z-up world coordinates in meters. The lines and saved camera are authored inputs; the page does not generate annotations from IFC properties.

bcf.load() reads the saved topic identifier, viewer.add() imports the original archive bytes, and viewer.selectTopic() restores the annotated view. The SDK renders the model and annotations together. Restoring the view reuses the imported topic. Retry sample retains completed imports.

Copy this folder and serve it over HTTP, for example python -m http.server 8080. The published SDK and full model download require internet access.

examples.title: Switch between projects on a map
examples.description: Choose a project to replace the loaded model and move the map to its location in the same viewer.
examples.guideHtml:
Switch between projects on a map

Choose a project to replace the loaded model and move the map to its location in the same viewer.

Try it

  1. Zürich district opens with the map enabled. Choose Rotterdam bridge to replace it and move to the Netherlands.
  2. Choose Zürich district to switch back. Only the selected project's model is loaded.
  3. Open View at the top right → Layers and choose Street or Satellite.
  4. Select a component, then click 1 element selected at the top left to open Properties.

Developer integration

Create one Viewer and await viewer.ready. For each project change, await viewer.clear(), download the selected IFC, await viewer.add(), then await viewer.toggleMap(true). Clearing releases the previous project's models and geographic context; enabling the map after import uses the new project's coordinates. The host never disables the map between projects or creates another viewer. Project controls are disabled during the transition to prevent overlapping imports. Download, import and map errors use the SDK message API; choose either project to retry.

Geographic placement

Both complete IFC files are imported unchanged and have native map conversions. Zürich uses Swiss LV95 (EPSG:2056) and LN02 heights, including model terrain. Rotterdam's Van Brienenoord bridge uses Amersfoort / RD New (EPSG:28992). The bridge source does not declare a vertical datum; this example retains its original heights and does not claim survey-grade terrain alignment. The SDK owns map layers, attribution and geographic placement.
